title: How do we find the missing angles of a trapezium?
description: In a trapezium, a slanting side cuts the two parallel sides, so the two angles on one side of it add up to one hundred eighty degrees. Each missing angle is found by subtracting the known angle, and the four angles are added to check. Keeko doubts that opposite angles of a trapezium are equal.
teaching_notes: One idea: the two angles on the same side of a slanting side between parallel sides add up to one hundred eighty degrees. Watch for students who copy the parallelogram rule that opposite angles are equal.

source: Trapezium PQRS has PQ || SR, ∠P = 70° and ∠Q = 55°. Find ∠S and ∠R.
video_script.why: The child sees that the two angles on one side of a slanting side between parallel sides add up to 180 degrees, so each missing angle is 180 minus the known one.
video_script.substitution: the book's own trapezium PQRS with PQ parallel to SR, angle P of 70 degrees and angle Q of 55 degrees
video_script.anchor: the trapezium PQRS of the book with PQ parallel to SR
video_script.wrong_answer: angle R is seventy and angle S is fifty five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks angle R is seventy and angle S is fifty five by copying the parallelogram rule, but only one pair of sides is parallel.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle S is one hundred ten degrees and angle R is one hundred twenty five degrees

final_answer.spoken: angle S is one hundred ten degrees and angle R is one hundred twenty five degrees

never_show: opposite angles of the trapezium named equal
maths_rules: PQ is parallel to SR, and PS cuts both, so angle S + angle P = 180
QR cuts both parallel sides, so angle R + angle Q = 180, and angle R = 180 - 55 = 125
video_script.design: One idea: angles on the same side of a slanting side add up to 180. One trapezium stays on the board and each slanting side is lit in turn.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the trapezium PQRS with PQ and SR marked parallel, angle P of 70 degrees and angle Q of 55 degrees

marks.def: the trapezium appears with its parallel sides marked
marks.ang: the angles P and Q are written
marks.ask: angles S and R glow with question marks

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a trapezium.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is called a trapezium.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>In trapezium P Q R S, P Q is parallel to S R.
Angle P is seventy degrees, and angle Q is fifty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find angles S and R?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two parallel lines cut by a slanting line, with the two angles on one side of it marked and joined by a plus sign to 180 degrees

marks.cut: a slanting line cuts two parallel lines
marks.sum: the two angles on one side add up to one hundred eighty degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Take two parallel lines and a slanting line that cuts both.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The two angles on one side of the slanting line add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, trapezium P Q R S, with P Q parallel to S R.
Angle P is seventy degrees, and angle Q is fifty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find angles S and R.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: PQ ∥ SR and PS cuts both, so ∠S + ∠P = 180°

marks.par: the parallel sides P Q and S R light up
marks.side: the slanting side P S lights up
marks.sum: angles P and S are joined to one hundred eighty degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='par'/>Step one, P Q and S R are the parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='side'/>The slanting side P S cuts both of them.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Angles P and S are on the same side, so they add up to one hundred eighty degrees.

marks.sub: one hundred eighty minus seventy is written
marks.val: the value is written at corner S

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step two, angle S is one hundred eighty minus seventy.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That is one hundred ten degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: QR cuts both parallel sides, so ∠R + ∠Q = 180° and ∠R = 180 − 55 = 125°

marks.side: the slanting side Q R lights up
marks.sum: angles Q and R are joined to one hundred eighty degrees
marks.val: one hundred eighty minus fifty five is written at corner R

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Step three, the slanting side Q R also cuts both parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Angles Q and R add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Angle R is one hundred eighty minus fifty five, which is one hundred twenty five degrees.

marks.tot: the total three hundred sixty is written

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check by adding the four angles.
Seventy plus fifty five plus one hundred twenty five plus one hundred ten is three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The four angles of a four-sided shape add up to three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle S is one hundred ten degrees and angle R is one hundred twenty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the trapezium with 70 and 55 copied onto the opposite corners; the sum 70 + 55 + 70 + 55 = 250 appears; the copied angles are struck out

marks.doubt: seventy and fifty five are copied onto the opposite corners
marks.sum: the four angles are added and show two hundred fifty
marks.fix: only the parallel pair P Q and S R is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks angle R is seventy and angle S is fifty five.
Keeko copies the rule that opposite angles are equal.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Those four angles would add up to only two hundred fifty degrees.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That rule needs two pairs of parallel sides, and here only one pair is parallel.
